extracted.intended_audience: Small businesses preparing SBIR/STTR grant applications (applicants, PD/PIs, grant administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting the SBIR/STTR application components shown (budget sections and SBIR/STTR eligibility questions) and drafting the Commercialization Plan (market analysis, target market, outreach, and value).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget: Section A — Personnel (Total Salary, Wages and Fringe Benefits (A+B))
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel — Total Salary, Wages and Fringe Benefits (A+B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a required budget category (Section A) for reporting salary, wages, and fringe benefits for project personnel. No additional guidance in this chunk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget: Section C — Equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Section C, Equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required budget category to list equipment costs separately from other direct costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget: Section D — Travel (Domestic and Foreign)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section D, Travel: 1. Domestic 2. Foreign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Travel costs must be separated into domestic and foreign travel lines in the budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget: Section E — Participant/Trainee Support Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Section E, Participant/Trainee Support Costs including: 1. Tuition/Fees/Health Insurance 2. Stipends 3. Travel 4. Subsistence 5. Other 6. Number of Participants/Trainees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participant support costs (tuition, stipends, travel, subsistence, other) and the number of participants/trainees must be itemized under Section E.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget: Section F — Other Direct Costs (itemized)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section F, Other Direct Costs including: 1. Materials and Supplies 2. Publication Costs 3. Consultant Services 4. ADP/Computer Services 5. Subawards/Consortium/Contractual Costs 6. Equipment or Facility Rental/User Fees 7. Alterations and Renovations 8. Other 1 9. Other 2 10. Other 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other direct cost categories must be itemized; subawards and contractual costs reported here. (The form lists multiple 'Other' lines for additional items.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget: Section G — Direct Costs (A thru F)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section G, Direct Costs (A thru F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Total direct costs are computed by summing Sections A–F and reported in Section G.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget: Section H — Indirect Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Section H, Indirect Costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indirect (facilities & administrative) costs must be reported separately in Section H.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget: Section I — Total Direct and Indirect Costs (G + H)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section I, Total Direct and Indirect Costs (G + H).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Total project cost equals Direct Costs (G) plus Indirect Costs (H) and is reported in Section I.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget: Section J — Fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Section J, Fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicable, any fee/profit is reported in Section J.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR Program Type selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Program Type (select only one): SBIR, STTR, or Both. (See agency-specific instructions to determine whether a particular agency allows a single submission for both SBIR and STTR.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must choose one program type and follow agency-specific instructions regarding combined submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR Type selection (Phase I/Phase II/Fast-Track)
rubrics_metrics.description: SBIR/STTR Type (select only one): Phase I, Phase II, Fast-Track. (See agency-specific instructions to determine whether a particular agency participates in Fast-Track.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must indicate the phase of the SBIR/STTR application and consult agency rules for Fast-Track participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: Small business certification at time of award (Question 1a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you certify that at the time of award your organization will meet the eligibility criteria for a small business as defined in the funding opportunity announcement? (Yes/No)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must certify small business eligibility at time of award per the funding opportunity announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated number of personnel at time of award (Question 1b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipated Number of personnel to be employed at your organization at the time of award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a numeric estimate of personnel count at award time as part of eligibility reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of subcontracts with Federal laboratories/agencies (Question 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does this application include subcontracts with Federal laboratories or any other Federal Government agencies? If yes, insert the names of the Federal laboratories/agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must disclose any subcontracting relationships with Federal labs/agencies and name them if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: HUBZone status disclosure (Question 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are you located in a HUBZone? (Refer to SBA mapping utility.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must indicate HUBZone status and may consult the SBA tool to determine eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic performance of R&D (Question 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Will all research and development on the project be performed in its entirety in the United States? If no, provide an explanation in an attached file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must certify that R&D will be performed in the U.S.; if not, include an explanation as an attachment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of essentially equivalent proposals/awards (Question 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Has the applicant and/or PD/PI submitted proposals for essentially equivalent work under other Federal program solicitations or received other Federal awards for essentially equivalent work? If yes, insert the names of the other Federal agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must disclose duplicate/substantially equivalent submissions or awards to other federal agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure permission statement for unsuccessful applications (Question 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: If this application does not result in an award, is the Government permitted to disclose the title of your proposed project, and the name, address, telephone number and e-mail address of the official signing for the applicant organization, to organizations that may be interested in contacting you for further information? (Yes/No)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant indicates whether contact information and project title may be shared by the Government if the application is not funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercialization Plan requirement for Phase II / Fast-Track (Question 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercialization Plan: If you are submitting a Phase II or Phase I/Phase II Fast-Track Application, include a Commercialization Plan in accordance with the agency announcement and/or agency-specific instructions. (Attach File)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A commercialization plan is mandatory for Phase II and Fast-Track submissions and must follow agency-specific instructions; attach the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR-specific: Prior SBIR Phase II awards and commercialization history (Question 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Have you received SBIR Phase II awards from the Federal Government? If yes, provide a company commercialization history in accordance with agency-specific instructions using the attachment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the company has prior SBIR Phase II awards, include a commercialization history attachment per agency instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR-specific: PI primary employment with small business at time of award (Question 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the Project Director/Principal Investigator have his/her primary employment with the small business at the time of award? (Yes/No)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For SBIR applications, indicate whether the PD/PI's primary employment will be with the small business at award time (affects eligibility/commitment).

rubrics_metrics.name: STTR-specific: PI appointment/commitment and minimum 10% effort requirement (Question 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Please indicate whether the answer to BOTH of the following questions is TRUE: (1) Does the PD/PI have a formal appointment or commitment either with the small business directly (as an employee or a contractor) OR as an employee of the Research Institution, which in turn has made a commitment to the small business through the STTR application process; AND (2) Will the PD/PI devote at least 10% effort to the proposed project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both conditions must be true for STTR: formal appointment/commitment AND at least 10% effort by the PD/PI.

rubrics_metrics.name: STTR-specific: Allocation of work between small business and research institution (Question 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the joint research and development proposed in this project, does the small business perform at least 40% of the work and the research institution named in the application perform at least 30% of the work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STTR requires minimum thresholds for percent effort/share of work: small business ≥40% and research institution ≥30%.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercialization Plan: Explicit goals / required content (as stated)
rubrics_metrics.description: The goals of this commercialization plan are to provide information regarding US gonorrhea infections, identify the target market for vaccine commercialization, address market strategy, discuss industry outreach efforts, and measure the value such a vaccine would have for both health organizations and TherapyXInc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercialization Plan should explicitly cover epidemiology (U.S. infections), target market identification, market strategy, industry outreach, and the value proposition to health organizations and the company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercialization Plan: Market analysis content (disease burden, epidemiology, treatment/resistance, costs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Market Analysis should document disease overview (incidence, prevalence, at-risk groups), complications, occurrence patterns (age/sex/location/race/SES), diagnosis and treatment landscape, antimicrobial resistance trends, treatment centers and reporting sources, and economic burden (screening, diagnosis, treatment, sequelae costs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan in this application includes detailed epidemiology, treatment/resistance history, diagnostic and treatment costs, treatment center reporting patterns, and estimates of economic burden — indicating these are expected components of a commercialization-market analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercialization Plan: Product description and intended use
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the lead product (example: GvaX12® — nanoencapsulated IL-12 plus outer membrane vesicles formulated for mucosal delivery), intended mechanism (enhance adaptive immune responses), and intended indication (vaccine for genital tract N. gonorrhoeae infection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercialization plans should include a clear product description, formulation, mechanism of action, and intended clinical indication/benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercialization Plan: Justification for vaccine investment (public health rationale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide justification for vaccine development based on public health threat (antimicrobial resistance, rising incidence, complications, and limited treatment options), and explain how vaccines can reduce antibiotic use and provide herd immunity benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong commercialization plan must argue the public health need and potential impact of a vaccine, including data on resistance trends and limitations of current therapies.
